_meta.description: APRA CRE property categories, sub-classifications, and general definitions. Authoritative reference for all Oney tools.
_meta.usage: Import via <script src='data/apra-definitions.json'> or fetch(). Access via window.APRA_DATA or OneyData.apra

propertyCategories.name: Office
propertyCategories.description: Commercial office space, typically used for professional/service providers.

propertyCategories.name: Retail
notes: Gyms should be treated as retail

propertyCategories.name: Industrial
propertyCategories.description: Properties used for manufacturing and/or storage and distribution. A building used predominately for industrial purposes, whether or not part of the building is used for ancillary purposes.
notes: Car/truck dealerships fall under 'Retail'
Car/truck parking areas fall under 'Other'

propertyCategories.name: Tourism & Leisure
propertyCategories.description: Properties associated with the tourism and leisure industry.
notes: For a T&L property to be considered CRE, the entire building should be rented under third party agreement with servicing of the debt reliant on a fixed annual rent rather than performance of the business.
Gyms should be treated as retail

propertyCategories.name: Other
propertyCategories.description: Property not associated with any other property type.
examples: Education related properties (including schools and universities)
Medical Facilities (including Medical Centres, doctor surgeries, day surgeries)
Rural Property (where the rural property was specifically acquired for lease or resale)
notes: Where a property is mixed use, the property type should be selected based on the predominant portion on the basis of MV or market rent.

propertyCategories.name: Other Residential
propertyCategories.description: Residential properties comprising four or more units on one site.
examples: Apartment blocks less than or equal to 3 storeys
notes: The number of storeys does not include basement levels.

propertyCategories.name: Land Development & Subdivision
propertyCategories.description: Land or sites acquired for the purpose of subdivision or development.

subTypes.name: Englobo Land / Land Banking
subTypes.description: Land that is undeveloped, largely unserviced, zoned/unzoned but held with the intent for future subdivision into smaller lots for residential, commercial or industrial use, and is typically subject to elongated holding or selling periods.
notes: No funding commitment to subdivide into individual lots – debt servicing from other revenue sources

subTypes.name: Pre-Development Sites
subTypes.description: Land held with the intent of building construction with/without Development Approval.
notes: No funding commitment for development – debt servicing from other sources

subTypes.name: Land Sub-Division - Single Stage
subTypes.description: Funding commitment to sub-divide / land currently being sub-divided in a single stage with < 50 lots.

subTypes.name: Land Sub-Division - Multi Stage
subTypes.description: Funding commitment to sub-divide / land currently being sub-divided in multiple stages. Also includes single stage subdivisions >= 50 lots.

notes: In the case of Pre-development sites where development/construction finance has been approved then the property category must reflect the property category applicable at the completion of building/development – e.g. Office, Industrial etc. Property Use in eBL = Development.

importantRules.description: If an investment facility is secured by more than one property, the property type in the commercial property tab in eBL should reflect the predominant property type of all direct and indirect commercial securities.
Where a property is mixed use, the property type should be selected based on the predominant portion on the basis of MV or market rent.

residentialDevelopmentDefinitions.name: Traditional Developments
residentialDevelopmentDefinitions.definition: A professional developer, selling sufficient product to clear debt.

residentialDevelopmentDefinitions.name: Speculative Developments
residentialDevelopmentDefinitions.definition: A professional developer who can't, or does not want to, get pre-sales and is backing themselves to sell the product at a later stage.
notes: These should only be considered for our well established and experienced developers.

residentialDevelopmentDefinitions.name: Build to Rent
residentialDevelopmentDefinitions.definition: Significant scale (400 units+) mainly used by IB customers which are essentially un-serviced apartments (i.e. they have one site management, dry cleaning services, maintenance etc.).
notes: Minimum 400 units
Single site management model

residentialDevelopmentDefinitions.name: Build to Hold
residentialDevelopmentDefinitions.definition: A non-professional developer who wants to hold 100% of the stock as a passive long-term investment.
characteristics: Inability to claim GST on construction
Need to use income to service the investment transaction
Possible recourse to alternate income streams

residentialDevelopmentDefinitions.name: Wealth Generation
residentialDevelopmentDefinitions.definition: A non-professional developer doing a smaller size development which is not their core business, don't want pre-sales, but will sell at the right price.
characteristics: Have recourse to alternate income streams
Form an integral part of the Bank's portfolio

officeGrades.source: Property Council of Australia (PCA) office buildings classifications

grades.name: Premium Grade
grades.description: Landmark office buildings with expansive views or outlook, ample natural lighting, prestige lobby and finishes, high quality access from an attractive street setting and premium maintenance.

criteria.lifts: Specific performance requirements apply to all classifications with different service requirements
amenities: Carpark with loading docks or delivery bays
criteria.sustainability: 5 Star Green Star Design Rating including 5 Star NABERS Office Energy rating commitment

grades.name: A-Grade
grades.description: High quality with good views, outlook and natural light, good quality access from an attractive street setting and high quality maintenance.

amenities: Carpark with loading docks or delivery bays
criteria.sustainability: 4 Star Green Star Design Rating including 4.5 Star NABERS Office Energy rating commitment

grades.name: B-Grade
grades.description: Quality office space with a good standard of finish and maintenance.

criteria.sustainability: 4 Star Green Star Design Rating including 4 Star NABERS Office Energy rating commitment

grades.name: C-Grade
grades.description: Office assets that do not meet Premium, A or B-Grade definitions, generally of average quality space with lifts.

grades.name: D-Grade
grades.description: Office assets that are not accommodated in the other categories, of lesser quality and no lift.

notes: Strata Office: where a strata office encompasses an entire floor plate, the building grade for the underlying building may be adopted. Where this is not the case, the grading should be assessed solely on the characteristics of the area being taken as security.
Major CBDs: Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane, Perth

retailCentreDefinitions.name: Strips / Shops
retailCentreDefinitions.description: Strip shops which do not meet Bulky assets/Large Format centres, Neighbourhood Retail or Focus asset criteria.
examples: Restaurants (including cafes & fast food outlets etc.)
Auto Service Centre (tyres, service, repairs etc.)

retailCentreDefinitions.name: Bulky Goods
retailCentreDefinitions.description: Bulky good retailers occupying large areas (generally >1,500 sqm) to display merchandise, e.g. furniture, electrical, whitegoods, homewares etc.

retailCentreDefinitions.name: Large Format Centres
retailCentreDefinitions.description: A medium to large sized shopping centre dominated by bulky goods retailers.
criteria: Generally located adjacent to large regional centre or in non-traditional retail locations (e.g. greenfield sites and industrial areas)

retailCentreDefinitions.name: Regional Shopping Centre
retailCentreDefinitions.description: Major integrated centre under a single management.
criteria: At least one department store or discount department store (DDS) of a min. 10,000 sqm GLA, AND the centre contains total GLA in excess of 25,000 sqm
OR three full line DDSs or equivalent each of min. 5,000 sqm GLA, AND the centre contains total reporting GLA in excess of 50,000 sqm

retailCentreDefinitions.name: Sub Regional Shopping Centre
retailCentreDefinitions.description: Centre built around one or two major DDSs, one or more supermarkets, and includes speciality shops.

retailCentreDefinitions.name: Neighbourhood Centre
retailCentreDefinitions.description: Centre less than 10,000 sqm in size.
criteria: A collection of food and non-food speciality shops and services
Typically includes at least one Food and Grocery anchor tenant of >400 sqm or only one DDS which is smaller than 4,000 sqm

specialisedPropertyDefinitions.description: Specialised property is property that is purpose-built or used for a specific purpose. When considering specialised asset class transactions, a deeper understanding of the risk profile needs to be contemplated before presenting structures to your clients.

subTypes.name: Medical Clinics
notes: A Medical Clinic is a collection of Medical Services on the same site (e.g. GP, Pharmacist, Pathology, Radiation). Generally housed in purpose built premises with limited alternative use. Treated as 'Specialised - Commercial'.

A General Practice Clinic provides healthcare to local community outpatients only. Operates from commercial offices/units or renovated residential. Where zoning allows mixed use and conversion at minimal cost, bankers may seek DCA Level 3 approval to treat as normal 'Commercial' property.

subTypes.name: Education
examples: Education related properties (including schools and universities)

subTypes.name: Type 1 - Permanent plantings and horticulture
examples: Nuts (almonds, cashews, chestnuts, macadamia, pecans, walnuts)

generalDefinitions.definition: Certain property income means pre-tax rental from the current term of committed leases (excluding lease term extension options) less non-recoverable outgoings (excluding capital expenditure).
Is issued by the local council or builder surveyor to a developer to confirm that a commercial or residential building is at a stage where it is safe to occupy.
notes: Must be presented with the final progressive payment request of a construction/development loan.

generalDefinitions.definition: A certificate the builder gets the customer to sign before handing over the completed house. The certificate is the customer's acceptance that all identified problems have been fixed and the building works have been completed.
Issued to the builder by the project architect, engineer, etc. to confirm that the works under the construction or development contract have reached the stage of completion.
notes: Care: The certificate does not mean that the building is compliant with relevant Commonwealth, state and local government legislation (e.g. a residential aged care facility might not have passed fire safety standards as part of their accreditation).

generalDefinitions.definition: Construction cost is calculated as construction / development cost of the physical construction.
Cost to complete is the amount to be spent on a project (including financing costs) to bring it to practical completion.
The debt servicing group includes the borrowing entities within an aggregation group that are linked because of a common reliance on cash flows for debt servicing and/or repayment.
A written guarantee issued by a financial institution that substitutes the 10% cash deposit traditionally required to purchase a property.

The lease of land alone, sometimes secured by improvements built on the land. A means used to separate the ownership of the land from the ownership of the buildings and improvements constructed on the land.
generalDefinitions.riskNote: Ground leases add complexity — lender must assess both land lease terms and building ownership structure.

generalDefinitions.definition: Contained within local council planning schemes and assist in protecting the heritage of a municipality. May not apply to the whole of a heritage place (i.e. it could apply to the external paint controls of a building only). Are listed in each state or territory's Heritage Register and could include a diverse range of places, buildings and objects (including Aboriginal places, buildings, objects, monuments, gardens, natural landscapes, archaeological sites, shipwrecks, relics, streets, industrial structures, public buildings, shops, factories, houses, religious buildings, schools, conservation precincts, jetties, bridges and movable items such as church organs and ferries).
generalDefinitions.riskNote: Heritage overlays restrict modification and development potential. Automatic amber flag in security assessment.

generalDefinitions.definition: The point in time when: (1) work for the building construction or development has been completed; all equipment has been installed, tested and found to be in running order; and the project is deemed safe for occupation by the issuer of the Certificate of Practical Completion / Certificate of Occupancy; AND (2) builder seeks the final progress payment claim.

Calculated as the lower of: the payout of the existing financier; OR purchase price of the property site on the contract of sale; PLUS stamp duty costs and legal fees, council contributions, consultation and professional fees, project manager fees, demolition cost, construction/development costs, advertising and marketing fees, holding costs, project contingency costs, fit-out costs, builders margin allowance, interest using the Bank's calculated estimate, and any other costs.
notes: Loan to cost ratio is calculated at a project level.
components: Stamp duty costs and legal fees

standard.label: Standard
standard.description: Most lenders comfortable with this property type

elevated.label: Elevated
elevated.description: Fewer lenders, stricter conditions, specialist assessment required

high.label: High
high.description: Limited lender appetite, typically requires development finance specialist
